title: Halting from an answer state
statement: Let $a,b,f,B\in\mathbb{N}$, let $m\in\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$, let $o$ be an oracle on five Boolean words, and let $y$ be a Boolean word. For any register record $st$ whose fifteen entries are at most $B$ and either Boolean $r$, the machine $A(a,b,f,m)$ on input $y$, started at its answer-$r$ state with register values $st$ and no result recorded, halts with result $r$; at every earlier time its configuration satisfies the guard requiring its prescribed precondition and all register values to be at most $B$.
hypotheses_covered: $o$ is an oracle on five Boolean words
Every one of the fifteen entries of $st$ is at most $B$
replaced:
Let $a,b,f,B$ be natural numbers, let $m$ be a Boolean mode, let $o$ be an oracle on
five Boolean-word inputs, and let $y$ be a Boolean word. If a state $st$ has all fifteen
register values at most $B$, then for either Boolean $r$, the machine $A(a,b,f,m)$ on
input $y$, started in the state labeled by answer $r$ with register vector $st$ and no
recorded result, halts with result $r$; at every earlier time its configuration
satisfies the guard requiring the prescribed precondition and all registers to be at
most $B$.
